summary: Oregon's only offshore lighthouse: built 1879-81 on a basalt rock 1.2 miles off Tillamook Head, battered by storms until the Coast Guard closed it in 1957; now private.

structures.type: square tower rising from the keepers' dwelling

access.note: Privately owned and part of the Oregon Islands National Wildlife Refuge; the 1980 nomination says access was by helicopter only. No public landing.

events.note: Surveyor John R. Trewaves killed in a landing attempt
Construction begun October 1879 under Charles A. Ballantyne
Cornerstone laid in June (22nd or 24th, sources differ)
British bark Lupatia lost on Tillamook Head, 3 January
Storm of 9 December 1894 destroyed 13 lantern panes and damaged the lens and roofs
Telegraph cable laid between rock and shore by tender Manzanita (fiscal year ended June 1896)
New concrete roof and second storey (1898 by the nomination's description; 1889 by its significance statement)
Storm of 18-19 October 1912: lantern pane broken, light out for about 15 minutes
Storm of 21-25 October 1934: 16 lantern panes broken, derrick lost, radio improvised
Three sick men taken off by breeches buoy to the tender Rose, 1 December 1934
Emergency repairs completed end of January 1935; new derrick
Steel mesh storm guard added around the lantern
Lighthouse Service absorbed by the Coast Guard; principal keepers remained civilian
Last log entry 1 September 1957; replaced by a whistle buoy
Offered for sale by the General Services Administration
Bought by Mimi Morissette; converted to the Eternity at Sea Columbarium

The Light-House Board's 1895 report says plans for a stronger roof were still being prepared, which fits 1898. The story states the disagreement.
24 June 1880 (nomination) versus 22 June 1880 (Oregon Encyclopedia, OHS finding aid). Story states both.

notes_for_editor: Evidence base: NRHP nomination (1980), Oregon Encyclopedia (own words only), Light-House Board reports 1895-1900, Lighthouse Service Bulletins 1913, 1922, 1930, 1934, 1935, Commissioner 1922, USLHS roster. Not read: Gillespie's 1881 construction report (HathiTrust, off-limits), Lighthouse Board report for 1881, Gibbs's books, Portland/Astoria newspapers. NRHP spells Trewaves/Ballantyne; OE Trewavas/Ballentyne. Roster 'at least 1956-' Coast Guard names have no end year. Dahlgren and Gerlof dates in OE/OHS summaries (Dahlgren 1901-1919 or 1901-1909; Gerloff 1903-1928) differ from the register (assistants first); story follows the register. Distance to Columbia River entrance is 17, 18 or 20 miles by source. The Lupatia crew count differs among web accounts (16 vs 23); NRHP says only 'entire crew', so no number given. Manzanita cable year: the 1896-97 volume's tender section covers the fiscal year ended June 1896 (inferred from 'spring of 1896' and 'October 1895'). Bulletin 1913 and 1934/35 OCR is column-interleaved; evidence quotes are single-line fragments. Bulletin 1924 (storm of late October, seas broke two lantern panes) was left out because OCR columns were scrambled. Current ownership: the 2022 sale listing and 2023 landing reported by Oregonlive could not be read (403), so Today relies on the 1980 nomination and the Oregon Encyclopedia; an editor should check current ownership and access. First assistant keeper Hammond 'F. C.' per Bulletin, 'Frank C. Hammond' per roster (matched by name and station only). Fiscal-year note: the 1894 storm appears in the report for the year ended June 1895 and is dated by the report itself. Checker: nomination's 'seventeen years' of Las Vegas ownership before 1973 conflicts with its 1959 sale date; Allik 'twenty years' vs register 1952-57; both now stated in text.
